title: Case: Brewery receives a delivery reminder for a day it thought had been moved
context: Three pallets of empty glass bottles are travelling from a glassworks to a brewery with Plover Arc freight. The desk has coordinated the delivery booking between the shipper, the carrier and the brewery since late January.
initial_request: Just had a reminder from Plover Arc saying BP-6970 is TOMORROW at 7?! The yard's dug up tomorrow, there's literally no surface for a lorry. I thought we were Thursday 10 to 12? Did someone undo it when we said no to the early one? Which is it, I need to tell the crew today and stop a lorry turning up to a hole in the ground.

Can you coordinate the delivery booking with Plover Arc freight and Fenmore's receiving? Callie Brennan is their contact.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Callie Brennan, Fenmore Brewing Co receiving coordinator
acceptable_actions.summary: The live booking is BP-6972, Thursday 12 Feb, 10:00–12:00; BP-6970 was cancelled on 3 Feb and the reminder comes from its old record; declining BP-6974 left BP-6972 unchanged.

must: Sends one message to Callie Brennan on the Business portal about DL-6970.
Tells her the live booking is BP-6972, Thursday 12 February, 10:00 to 12:00 (UK time is the same as UTC in February), and that BP-6970 for Tuesday was cancelled on 3 February.
Explains that the reminder comes from the cancelled booking's record, which the Freight planner warned can still send reminders, and that declining the early BP-6974 slot left BP-6972 unchanged.
must_not: Tells her the delivery is tomorrow, Tuesday 10 February, or treats BP-6970 as live.
Gives BP-6974 or 07:00 to 09:00 on Thursday as the booking.
Promises an exact arrival time inside the 10:00 to 12:00 window.
expected.reference_message: Hi Callie, you're right, it's Thursday. The only live booking for DL-6970 is BP-6972, Thursday 12 February, 10:00–12:00. Plover Arc cancelled BP-6970 (Tuesday) on 3 February, and when you turned down the early BP-6974 slot on the 5th they confirmed BP-6972 was unchanged. Their Freight planner warned that the portal can still send reminders from a cancelled booking's record, which is what this one is, so nothing is booked for tomorrow. Please ignore any reminder that isn't BP-6972.

rationale: Event 23 is the Freight planner's confirmation: BP-6972 on Thursday 12 February is the only live booking, BP-6970 is cancelled, and stale reminders can still fire from the old record. The later early-slot offer BP-6974 was declined and withdrawn, leaving BP-6972 unchanged. The reminder is exactly the stale message the planner warned of, so the desk answers the brewery today from the confirmed booking.
trap: Treats the newest event, an automated reminder for BP-6970 tomorrow, as current and tells the brewery to expect the lorry on Tuesday, or confuses the withdrawn early slot BP-6974 with the live booking.
basis: AIF-21 (lost in the middle: the decisive booking confirmation near the centre of a long thread, with later automated noise) and RULER multi-key needles with distractors https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.06654 . Booking systems that keep sending reminders from cancelled records are a familiar defect (UNVERIFIED as a statistic).

review.note: Blind answer matched: tell the brewery the reminder comes from cancelled BP-6970 and BP-6972 on Thursday 10:00-12:00 is live. A check with the Freight planner instead would leave her without an answer today despite its written confirmation and warning, so the key is not too narrow.
